changes.reason: THE-SILENT-EXPIRY: ServiceAccountService.UpdateForActor assigned ExpiresAt on the aggregate while the repository's UPDATE statement covered {name, description, role} only, so a PUT carrying just expires_at answered 200 and stored nothing — the account went on minting tokens past the expiry its operator had set. The statement now writes expires_at, and the rule pins the whole behaviour: the SET list names the column, an expiry-only update is stored and read back, a past expiry is refused without a write, and an unrelated update leaves the expiry standing. Mutation red-proved against the rule's mirrored column list; the shipped statement is additionally proved against a live database by a new integration tooth that writes an expiry through the repository and reads it back from the column

THE-SILENT-EXPIRY closes the third and last reader of the collapse THE-OWNERLESS-ACCOUNT fixed on the other two: ValidateBindingForClient mapped ANY store error to not-found, and the client create and update handlers mapped every service error to 400 invalid request, so a database outage told the operator their request was invalid. The validator now separates the store's TYPED verdict from an outage and both handlers answer 503 with a correlation id for the outage class. Mutation red-proved at the service seam and on the real POST /api/v1/clients route
